report.tagline: A free, game-like app for learning languages, maths, music and chess in short daily lessons.
report.simpleSummary: Duolingo turns learning a language into a mobile game. Lessons take about five minutes, you earn points, climb leagues and keep a daily streak going, and a green owl nudges you if you forget. It is free with ads, and about 1 in 12 monthly users pays for Super to remove ads and get extras like AI video calls. In 2025 its CEO said it would be 'AI-first', which caused a backlash, and in 2026 it chose to grow users even if it meant earning less in the short run.

overview.whatItDoes: Duolingo teaches over 40 languages plus maths, music and chess through short, game-like lessons. It uses AI to create courses, personalise practice and power features like Video Call with the character Lily. It also runs the Duolingo English Test, an online English exam accepted by thousands of universities.
howItWorks: You download the app, pick a language and a daily goal, and take a placement test.
Each lesson is a few minutes of tapping, typing and speaking exercises.
You earn XP, keep a daily streak and compete in weekly leagues.
Free users see ads and have limited energy for lessons; Super subscribers get no ads and unlimited practice.
Notifications and the owl mascot remind you to practise every day.
Duolingo runs hundreds of A/B tests to tune every screen for learning and retention.

businessModel.summary: Duolingo makes money from four things: Super subscriptions (most of it), ads shown to free users, the Duolingo English Test, and in-app purchases like streak repairs. It is a freemium app: most users never pay, and their activity is paid for by the few who do.

revenueStreams.detail: $270 million in Q3 2026, up 18%. Max is being folded into Super.
$20.8 million in Q3 2026, shown to free users.
Gems, streak repairs and items, $6.9 million in Q3 2026, down 38%.

businessModel.pricing: Free with ads and limited energy. Super about $12.99 a month or about $84 a year in the US, with lower prices in India and other markets. Family plan for up to 6 people. Duolingo English Test about $70.
costDrivers: AI computing for Video Call and personalised features, pushing gross margin toward 72%
App store fees from Apple and Google
Marketing and partnerships, like games tie-ins
businessModel.unitEconomics: Duolingo's yearly revenue of about $1.2 billion spread over 13 million paid subscribers is about $90 per subscriber a year. Apple or Google take up to 15% to 30% of in-app subscriptions, and AI and hosting cost more. Free users bring in only a few dollars a year from ads. Because most new users come free through word of mouth and social media, the cost to get a user is very low. So the business works as long as about 1 in 12 monthly users keeps paying. Rough estimates.

growth.moat: Duolingo has huge brand recognition, years of learning data from billions of exercises, and a habit system tuned by thousands of experiments. Its biggest asset is that tens of millions of people have a streak they do not want to lose. AI makes language teaching cheaper for rivals, so the habit and brand matter more than content.

pmLessons: Habit loops like streaks, leagues and reminders can drive retention better than content alone.
How you talk about AI matters. A memo about replacing people with AI cost Duolingo goodwill, even as AI improved the product.
Sometimes it is right to earn less now to grow users. Duolingo traded some bookings for faster DAU growth in 2026.
A freemium model works only if the free product is good enough to build the habit, and the paid one clearly better.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Duolingo's north star metric and why?
interviewQuestions.hint: DAUs. Explain how daily habit leads to learning and payment. Break into new, current, resurrected users.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase paid conversion without hurting DAUs?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment users, find value moments (Video Call, out of energy), test offers, use DAUs as a guardrail.

interviewQuestions.question: Users say Duolingo does not make them fluent. What would you build?
interviewQuestions.hint: Define fluency, add speaking practice, real-life tasks, measure learning outcomes, not just streaks.

interviewQuestions.question: ChatGPT can tutor languages for free. Is Duolingo in trouble?
interviewQuestions.hint: Separate teaching from motivation. Duolingo wins on habit, structure and brand. Show how it should use AI too.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to bring back lapsed users.
interviewQuestions.hint: Why they lapse, which triggers work, comeback rewards, new subjects. Metric: resurrected users.
